The diff does make the full test suite pass (I traced every test by hand: divisibility check, midnight wrap, and the round() call all line up), and the divisibility validation + `% MINUTES_PER_DAY` wrap are genuinely good, uncontroversial fixes.

However, the rounding change is a problem, and the PR description itself admits it: the docstring explicitly says "a time exactly halfway between two boundaries rounds up to the later one," but the implementation was switched to Python's `round()` (round-half-to-even) specifically because that's the only rule that satisfies both `test_halfway_rounds_up` (17.5 → 18, which happens to agree with "round up") and `test_morning_standup_half_hour_slot` (18.5 → 18, which contradicts "round up" and only works via round-to-even). The agent chose this implementation "only so that test_morning_standup_half_hour_slot passes" and flagged the docstring conflict as something that "should be reviewed" without actually resolving it — that's shipping code whose own documentation is now false, driven by reverse-engineering from the test suite rather than a confirmed spec.

Round-half-to-even is also a surprising choice for a room-booking slot snapper: two times that are both exactly halfway between two boundaries can now round in opposite directions depending on the parity of the slot index, which is not how "nearest slot, ties go later" is normally understood and will likely confuse whoever reads the docstring next.

Before merging, please either:
1. Confirm with the workplace team what the actual halfway tie-breaking rule is (since the current docstring appears to be wrong even before this PR), and update the docstring to accurately describe the real rule (e.g., round-half-to-even), or
2. If round-half-to-even truly is intended, at minimum rewrite the docstring so it no longer claims ties always round up.

Leaving the docstring and implementation contradicting each other is a real defect that should be fixed rather than merged silently, even though the tests themselves are untouched and green.
